blocks.label: 5 October update · 2026-10-05 · cutoff 21:28 UTC+8
blocks.placement: after existing R3 acknowledgment block; retain R3 unchanged
blocks.body: On 5 October, the public account of responsibility became more specific. CNA reported that police had given four officers two reprimands each for inappropriate language, had given the on-scene investigation chief a demerit for failing to intervene, and had given the precinct chief two reprimands for supervision. Read together here, the reported penalties give a more differentiated administrative account of language, intervention, and supervision; the original questions about taking people to the station as a group, their individual procedural status, and their experience of the encounter still require their own answers.
blocks.sourceNote: CNA published 15:11, updated 15:17; Liberty Times 14:51, Taiwan time. These are reporting timestamps. The disciplinary account is attributed to police; no complete administrative decisions or independent inquiry records were inspected.

blocks.label: 5 October update · 2026-10-05 · cutoff 21:28 UTC+8
blocks.placement: after existing R4 search/inspection distinction block; retain R4 unchanged
blocks.body: A later report returns to the question of how customers were taken to the station. NOWnews, in a report published at 16:21:50 Taiwan time, quotes police as saying there was no compulsory power requiring people to be taken away, and reports that police still needed to confirm what customers had been told. This account leaves a further question: how was the possibility of declining made available to each person at the scene? The report adds a police explanation to the record; it does not establish what every customer was told or how each person's movement was constrained.
blocks.sourceNote: NOWnews, 5 October 16:21:50 Taiwan time. The paragraph attributes the account to that report, without treating a news quotation as a legal ruling or a complete record of individual consent.

blocks.label: 5 October update · 2026-10-05 · cutoff 21:28 UTC+8
blocks.placement: after existing R7 records/visibility block; retain R7 unchanged
blocks.body: By evening, the reporting also became more personally specific. FTNN identified one officer by surname, Zhuang, and by his station, Juguang; NOWnews subsequently cited that report and quoted the precinct declining to comment on the report. These reports share a source chain. They do not independently establish the allegations about earlier conduct, and no reliable full-name identification was established in this update's source check. A surname-and-station description may become a focal point for public attention, but that partial identification cannot substitute for reconstructing the command, procedures, and opportunities to intervene in this operation.
blocks.sourceNote: FTNN 18:22; NOWnews 20:10:07, updated 20:10:34, 5 October Taiwan time. The Chinese identification is 莊姓員警; Zhuang is a surname transliteration, not a verified full legal name. Older alleged acts are not repeated as proven facts. Declining comment is not treated as confirmation.
